task_metadata.research_topic: conditional average treatment effect estimation from observational data
task_metadata.research_question: Design a novel estimator for conditional average treatment effects from observational data that is accurate, robust to confounding, and generalizes across explicitly synthetic benchmark families with different data-generating processes.
notes: Baseline and benchmark mappings were grounded in the task description plus comments/docstrings in edits/custom_template.py.
The test settings are task-local synthetic DGPs inspired by IHDP, Jobs/LaLonde, and ACIC rather than official benchmark datasets or released benchmark configurations.

tests.label: ihdp_synth
tests.notes: Synthetic observational DGP inspired by IHDP-style CATE benchmarks; not the official IHDP benchmark setting.

tests.label: jobs_synth
tests.notes: Synthetic job-training-style DGP inspired by Jobs/LaLonde program-evaluation benchmarks; not the official LaLonde/NSW dataset setting.

tests.label: acic_synth
tests.notes: Synthetic high-dimensional CATE DGP inspired by ACIC simulation studies; not an official ACIC competition scenario.

baselines.name: s_learner
baselines.notes: Kunżel et al. formalize S-learner and T-learner meta-learners for CATE estimation.

baselines.name: t_learner
baselines.notes: Kunżel et al. formalize S-learner and T-learner meta-learners for CATE estimation.

baselines.name: ipw
baselines.notes: The implementation is an IPW-style learner built around propensity weighting; Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983) is the canonical observational-causal reference for propensity score weighting rather than an exact one-to-one match to this specific code path.

baselines.name: causal_forest
baselines.notes: Direct match to the causal forest baseline.

baselines.name: dr_learner
baselines.notes: Direct match to Kennedy's modern doubly robust learner analysis referenced in the task description.

baselines.name: r_learner
baselines.notes: Direct match to the R-learner / residualization-based objective.
